claims.text: Localized friction stir processing of damaged Inconel 718 can repair microcracks.
Localized friction stir processing can eliminate hot-crack-sensitive phases in Inconel 718.
Friction stir processing induces dynamic recrystallization in Inconel 718.
Dynamic recrystallization produces a fine-grained, homogenized microstructure in the processed Inconel 718 region.
Friction stir processing causes dissolution or redistribution of hot-crack-sensitive phases.
Severe plastic deformation and controlled heat input during friction stir processing drive dynamic recrystallization.
Grain refinement and microstructural homogenization heal pre-existing microcracks.
The proposed processing mitigates the formation of deleterious phases in Inconel 718.
The FSP-treated repair region will have greater surface hardness than traditional fusion-weld repairs and untreated surfaces.
The FSP-treated repair region will have greater fatigue resistance than traditional fusion-weld repairs and untreated surfaces.
The FSP-treated repair region will have lower susceptibility to crack initiation and propagation than traditional fusion-weld repairs and untreated surfaces.
The FSP-treated surface will have improved wear resistance relative to traditional fusion-weld repairs and untreated surfaces.
The proposed intervention can be performed below 1100°C.
Performance gains depend on controlled tool travel speed and rotation rate that provide severe plastic deformation without overheating.
Deviations from the processing window or component geometries that cause inconsistent deformation may prevent the predicted performance gains.
Complex component geometries and tool wear may limit the effectiveness of localized FSP on Inconel 718.
